# FRAMEWORK-IMPROVEMENTS — suggestions for cap-evolve itself (cross-run)

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

## cand_0001
- Contradictory intake framing. The INSTRUCTIONS said "EMPTY SEED — create the capability from scratch (there are no files)" while `policy/policy.md`, `tools/tools.py`, and `reference/data_model.py` all existed and were non-empty. The "empty seed" block appears to be a stale template default that fires even when the seed is populated. Suggest gating that block on an actual `is_empty(dir)` check per capability so the optimizer isn't told to create files that already exist.
- Also contradictory: the summary block header placeholder literally rendered the "No actionable failures in focus …" sentence inside a code reference ("The `## No actionable failures…` block below summarizes them"), i.e. the template interpolated the no-failures banner into a spot meant to name the trajectory-summary section. Minor, but confusing.
- Un-winnable gate on a single-task val split at reward 1.000. With one val task already at 1.0, the hill-climb gate can never register an improvement, so every candidate this iteration is structurally destined to be rejected on val even if it strictly improves held-out generalization. Consider (a) surfacing this explicitly ("val is saturated; this iteration can only be judged on test"), and/or (b) letting the gate accept a non-regressing candidate when val is already maxed and the edit is well-supported, so generalization work isn't auto-discarded.
- tau2 was not importable in the candidate workdir, so `validate`/registration checks and `detect_loop_patterns.py` could not run. If the framework expects code-surface candidates to be validated, the runtime (tau2) should be importable in the work dir, or a lightweight stub provided.
